verdict.rationale: Independent hands-on reports describe the behavior the story asks for. LaunchDarkly clients download all flags in the project on connection and then stream changes over SSE, which adds no extra latency, and the Relay Proxy can run that streaming close to services. However, no first-party doc in the pack explicitly states that server SDKs evaluate locally from a cached ruleset, and Big Segments are fetched live from Redis (then cached) rather than evaluated purely locally. A 2016-era report of API lookup timeouts is ambiguous rather than a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of local in-memory evaluation in server SDKs, evidence of microsecond-level evaluation latency, and confirmation that no per-check network call occurs in every mode (Big Segments excepted).

support.subject: As a platform engineer, my server SDKs evaluate flags locally from a cached ruleset — microsecond decisions with no network call per flag check
